Actor

Actor is a Substrate-managed, agent-like workload instance, derived from an ActorTemplate. Substrate multiplexes many actors onto a small pool of workers by checkpointing an actor's guest state to a snapshot and restoring it on demand, rather than keeping every actor's worker running continuously - see SuspendActor, PauseActor, and ResumeActor.

MethodDescriptionRequestResponse
GetActor

Get an Actor.

 ateapi.GetActorRequest ateapi.Actor
CreateActor

Create a new Actor deriving from a given ActorTemplate.

 ateapi.CreateActorRequest ateapi.Actor
UpdateActor

Update mutable fields on an existing Actor.

 ateapi.UpdateActorRequest ateapi.Actor
SuspendActor

Suspend a given actor to a new snapshot. A running actor is checkpointed on its worker; a paused actor's node-local snapshot is uploaded, narrowed to the template's commit scope where required (Full capture, Data commit).

 ateapi.SuspendActorRequest ateapi.SuspendActorResponse
PauseActor

Pause a given actor and keep its snapshots on node VM.

 ateapi.PauseActorRequest ateapi.PauseActorResponse
ResumeActor

Resume an actor from its latest snapshot.

 ateapi.ResumeActorRequest ateapi.ResumeActorResponse
DeleteActor

Delete an actor. Only suspended actors can be deleted.

 ateapi.DeleteActorRequest ateapi.Actor
ListActors

List Actors.

 ateapi.ListActorsRequest ateapi.ListActorsResponse

+k8s:optional +k8s:maxItems=32 # matches the template's volumes bound +k8s:listType=map +k8s:listMapKey=volume_name

status.actor_volumes.volume_name string

Name of the volume specified in the actor template. Template volume names are DNS labels.

+k8s:required +k8s:format=k8s-short-name +k8s:update=NoModify +k8s:update=NoUnset # set-once; immutable would reject the create ratchet's nil->set when the final object is validated as an update

status.actor_volumes.storage_volume_id string

The globally unique volume_id returned from the storage system. This will be initially empty during volume creation. Its format is the storage system's own, so it is only bounded and checked for control characters (U+0000-U+0008, U+000B, U+000C, U+000E-U+001F, U+007F-U+009F). The CSI spec caps IDs at 128 bytes but does not require it, so allow some slack. Set once when provisioning completes, then never changed.

+k8s:optional +k8s:maxLength=256 +k8s:update=NoModify +k8s:update=NoUnset +k8s:customValidation # no control characters

status.actor_volumes.volume_type string

Internal volume plugin name or CSI driver name, from the StorageClass provisioner. Must be a DNS subdomain, optionally prefixed with "substrate.io/" (per the CSI spec's driver-name syntax).

+k8s:required +k8s:maxLength=253 +k8s:update=NoModify +k8s:update=NoUnset # set-once, like volume_name above +k8s:customValidation

status.actor_volumes.status ExternalVolume.Status

+k8s:optional +k8s:minimum=1 +k8s:maximum=3 # keep this in sync with the Status enum

status.actor_volumes.volume_context map<string, string>

volume_context contains metadata returned by the CSI driver during volume provisioning, needed by the node plugin for mounting (e.g. attachment info). Keys and values are the driver's own, so they are only bounded, not validated.

+k8s:optional +k8s:maxProperties=32 +k8s:eachKey=+k8s:maxLength=128 +k8s:eachVal=+k8s:maxLength=256

status.in_progress_local_snapshot_name string

The name of the in-progress node-local checkpoint. Like durable snapshot names, these are server-generated UUIDs.

+k8s:optional +k8s:format=k8s-short-name

status.current_actor_template_uid string

The UID of the actor template the Actor's guest state is currently built on: the one its latest sprint booted with, recorded when the resume (or first boot) commits RUNNING, or at creation for an Actor seeded from a tag, since that Actor borrows guest state that was already built. Empty means the Actor has no guest state yet. Diverges from the UID of the Actor's actor_template ref when a suspended Actor is repointed at a replacement template, which forces the next restore to data-only.

+k8s:optional

  },
  "actorTemplate": { "atespace": "prod", "name": "checkout-worker" },

    "state": "ACTOR_STATE_RUNNING",
    "workerAssignment": {
      "worker": { "name": "checkout-worker-pool-6b9d4f-x2p7q" },
      "workerNamespace": "substrate-workers",
      "workerPool": "checkout-worker-pool",
      "workerPod": "checkout-worker-pool-6b9d4f-x2p7q",
      "workerPodUid": "3c9e1a2b-6d4f-4b8e-9a71-2c5f0d8b3e94",
      "workerPodIp": "10.4.12.31"
    }
  }
}

The UID of the actor template the Actor's guest state is currently built on: the one its latest sprint booted with, recorded when the resume (or first boot) commits RUNNING, or at creation for an Actor seeded from a tag, since that Actor borrows guest state that was already built. Empty means the Actor has no guest state yet. SuspendActor

Suspend a given actor to a new snapshot. A running actor is checkpointed on its worker; a paused actor's node-local snapshot is uploaded, narrowed to the template's commit scope where required (Full capture, Data commit).

actor.status.actor_volumes.storage_volume_id string

The globally unique volume_id returned from the storage system. This will be initially empty during volume creation. Its format is the storage system's own, so it is only bounded and checked for control characters (U+0000-U+0008, U+000B, U+000C, U+000E-U+001F, U+007F-U+009F). The CSI spec caps IDs at 128 bytes but does not require it, so allow some slack. Set once when provisioning completes, then never changed.

+k8s:optional +k8s:format=k8s-short-name

actor.status.current_actor_template_uid string

The UID of the actor template the Actor's guest state is currently built on: the one its latest sprint booted with, recorded when the resume (or first boot) commits RUNNING, or at creation for an Actor seeded from a tag, since that Actor borrows guest state that was already built. Empty means the Actor has no guest state yet. Diverges from the UID of the Actor's actor_template ref when a suspended Actor is repointed at a replacement template, which forces the next restore to data-only.

+k8s:optional

actor.status.current_actor_template_uid string

The UID of the actor template the Actor's guest state is currently built on: the one its latest sprint booted with, recorded when the resume (or first boot) commits RUNNING, or at creation for an Actor seeded from a tag, since that Actor borrows guest state that was already built. Empty means the Actor has no guest state yet. Diverges from the UID of the Actor's actor_template ref when a suspended Actor is repointed at a replacement template, which forces the next restore to data-only.

+k8s:optional

resumed bool

True if a resume workflow was executed to activate the actor. False if the actor was already RUNNING.

+k8s:optional

actors.status.local_snapshot_info.snapshot_name string

The name of the local checkpoint on each of the nodes below. Checkpoint names are server-generated UUIDs, but any resource name is valid here.

+k8s:optional +k8s:format=k8s-short-name

actors.status.local_snapshot_info.node_vms_with_local_snapshots repeated string

Node VMs that have local snapshots for this actor, while it's PAUSED. Each node appears at most once.

TODO: revisit this design; a snapshot propagated to every node would grow this list with the fleet, and the bound below is provisional.

+k8s:optional +k8s:maxItems=256 +k8s:listType=set +k8s:eachVal=+k8s:format=k8s-long-name

actors.status.local_snapshot_info.content_scope SnapshotContentScope

Scope the pause checkpoint captured (the template's onPause at pause time). UNSPECIFIED is tolerated for compatibility and reads as FULL.

+k8s:optional +k8s:minimum=1 +k8s:maximum=2 # keep this in sync with the SnapshotContentScope enum

actors.status.actor_volumes repeated ExternalVolume

Volumes attached to the actor. These volumes only live as long as the actor. They are deleted when the actor is deleted. Each template volume appears at most once.

+k8s:optional +k8s:maxItems=32 # matches the template's volumes bound +k8s:listType=map +k8s:listMapKey=volume_name

actors.status.actor_volumes.volume_name string

Name of the volume specified in the actor template. Template volume names are DNS labels.

+k8s:required +k8s:format=k8s-short-name +k8s:update=NoModify +k8s:update=NoUnset # set-once; immutable would reject the create ratchet's nil->set when the final object is validated as an update

actors.status.actor_volumes.storage_volume_id string

The globally unique volume_id returned from the storage system. This will be initially empty during volume creation. Its format is the storage system's own, so it is only bounded and checked for control characters (U+0000-U+0008, U+000B, U+000C, U+000E-U+001F, U+007F-U+009F). The CSI spec caps IDs at 128 bytes but does not require it, so allow some slack. Set once when provisioning completes, then never changed.

+k8s:optional +k8s:maxLength=256 +k8s:update=NoModify +k8s:update=NoUnset +k8s:customValidation # no control characters

actors.status.actor_volumes.volume_type string

Internal volume plugin name or CSI driver name, from the StorageClass provisioner. Must be a DNS subdomain, optionally prefixed with "substrate.io/" (per the CSI spec's driver-name syntax).

+k8s:required +k8s:maxLength=253 +k8s:update=NoModify +k8s:update=NoUnset # set-once, like volume_name above +k8s:customValidation

actors.status.actor_volumes.status ExternalVolume.Status

+k8s:optional +k8s:minimum=1 +k8s:maximum=3 # keep this in sync with the Status enum

actors.status.actor_volumes.volume_context map<string, string>

volume_context contains metadata returned by the CSI driver during volume provisioning, needed by the node plugin for mounting (e.g. attachment info). Keys and values are the driver's own, so they are only bounded, not validated.

+k8s:optional +k8s:maxProperties=32 +k8s:eachKey=+k8s:maxLength=128 +k8s:eachVal=+k8s:maxLength=256

actors.status.in_progress_local_snapshot_name string

The name of the in-progress node-local checkpoint. Like durable snapshot names, these are server-generated UUIDs.

+k8s:optional +k8s:format=k8s-short-name

actors.status.current_actor_template_uid string

The UID of the actor template the Actor's guest state is currently built on: the one its latest sprint booted with, recorded when the resume (or first boot) commits RUNNING, or at creation for an Actor seeded from a tag, since that Actor borrows guest state that was already built. Empty means the Actor has no guest state yet. Diverges from the UID of the Actor's actor_template ref when a suspended Actor is repointed at a replacement template, which forces the next restore to data-only.

+k8s:optional

next_page_token string

Pagination token for the next page. Empty if this is the last page.

  }

Atespace

Atespace is the isolation boundary an Actor is created into. Global-scoped: metadata.atespace is always empty; the atespace's identity is metadata.name.

MethodDescriptionRequestResponse
CreateAtespace

Create a new Atespace. Substrate-native, stored in database.

 ateapi.CreateAtespaceRequest ateapi.Atespace
GetAtespace

Get an Atespace by name.

 ateapi.GetAtespaceRequest ateapi.Atespace
ListAtespaces

List Atespaces.

 ateapi.ListAtespacesRequest ateapi.ListAtespacesResponse
DeleteAtespace

Delete an empty Atespace. Rejects (FailedPrecondition) if any Actors or Tags remain.

 ateapi.DeleteAtespaceRequest ateapi.Atespace

EgressPolicy

EgressPolicy is an egress policy resource nested under an Actor. An Actor has at most one egress policy resource, named "default".

rules repeated EgressRule

Rules are evaluated in order. The first matching rule authorizes the request, only that rule's effects are applied, and evaluation stops even if later rules would also match. A request is denied when no rule matches.

+k8s:optional +k8s:maxItems=256 +k8s:listType=atomic # rule order matters

rules.hostnames HostnameRule

Matches when the request hostname matches any configured pattern. Effects are applied once when the rule matches.

+k8s:optional +k8s:unionMember

rules.hostnames.patterns repeated string

DNS names, or DNS names with a wildcard "*" in the leftmost label. The rule matches when any pattern matches.

The DNS name must conform to RFC 1034 and RFC 1123. It must be lowercase and must not have a trailing dot.

A wildcard replaces the complete leftmost label. "*.example.com" matches exactly one non-empty label, such as "api.example.com". It does not match "example.com" or "nested.api.example.com". No other wildcard syntax is accepted. A pattern without a wildcard matches only the complete normalized name.

Internationalized names must use their IDNA A-label (punycode) form; no Unicode conversion is performed. URLs, IP addresses, names with ports, malformed DNS names (for example, "foo..example.com"), and more than one trailing dot are invalid.

+k8s:required +k8s:maxItems=256 +k8s:listType=set +k8s:customValidation # format

rules.hostnames.effects EgressRuleEffects

Effects do not authorize traffic. They are applied only when this is the first matching rule.

+k8s:optional

rules.hostnames.effects.inject_static_headers repeated CredentialHeaderInjection

Injects values retrieved from credential providers into request headers. Header names must be unique case-insensitively.

+k8s:optional +k8s:maxItems=16 +k8s:listType=map +k8s:listMapKey=header +k8s:customUnique # case-insensitive +k8s:customValidation # for duplicate headers

rules.hostnames.effects.inject_static_headers.header string

The case-insensitive HTTP request header to inject.

+k8s:required +k8s:customValidation # format

rules.hostnames.effects.inject_static_headers.prefix string

Prepended verbatim to the credential value. Include any desired separator; for example, use "Bearer " (including the space) for Authorization.

+k8s:optional +k8s:customValidation # format

rules.hostnames.effects.inject_static_headers.credential_uri string

Source-agnostic reference interpreted by a registered credential provider: substrate-secret://<provider-class>/<provider-name>/<provider-specific-tail>

+k8s:required +k8s:customValidation # format

rules.cidrs CIDRRule

Matches when the original destination IP belongs to any configured prefix.

+k8s:optional +k8s:unionMember

rules.cidrs.cidrs repeated string

Canonical IPv4 or IPv6 CIDR prefixes. IPv4 uses dotted-decimal notation, such as "192.0.2.0/24". IPv6 uses lowercase compressed notation, such as "2001:db8::/32". Bits after the prefix length must be zero. The rule matches when the original destination IP belongs to any prefix.

+k8s:required +k8s:maxItems=256 +k8s:listType=set +k8s:customValidation # format

rules.all google.protobuf.Empty

Matches every destination.

+k8s:optional +k8s:unionMember

Tag

Tag is an Atespace-owned, stable name for one external snapshot. The external snapshot pointed by a tag is a copy of an actor snapshot. The snapshot is copied when the tag is created, and deleted when the tag is. Its owning Atespace cannot be deleted until the tag is removed.

MethodDescriptionRequestResponse
CreateTag

Tag the external snapshot a suspended Actor holds. The tag gets its own copy of that snapshot, so suspending or deleting the Actor afterwards cannot collect it.

 ateapi.CreateTagRequest ateapi.Tag
GetTag

Get a Tag.

 ateapi.GetTagRequest ateapi.Tag
ListTags

List Tags.

 ateapi.ListTagsRequest ateapi.ListTagsResponse
UpdateTag

Publish or unpublish a Tag without changing its address.

 ateapi.UpdateTagRequest ateapi.Tag
DeleteTag

Delete a Tag and the external snapshot it owns. Actors created from the tag that have not yet been suspended still point at that external snapshot and become unrecoverable, so do not delete a tag while such Actors exist.

 ateapi.DeleteTagRequest ateapi.Tag

CreateTag

Tag the external snapshot a suspended Actor holds. The tag gets its own copy of that snapshot, so suspending or deleting the Actor afterwards cannot collect it.

Parameters

tag Tag

The tag to create. metadata.atespace, metadata.name, scope and source_actor are honored; metadata.atespace must match source_actor's, and status is ignored on write.

+k8s:required

Worker

Worker is a schedulable worker pod.

Global-scoped: metadata.atespace is always empty. metadata.name is assigned by the control plane and is opaque to clients — never parse it or derive it from anything else; read pod identity from the named fields below.

labels is the only mutable field; every other field is either immutable after creation or output-only. UpdateWorker replaces the whole resource, so an immutable field that a request changes — including by omitting it, which would clear it — is rejected with INVALID_ARGUMENT.

MethodDescriptionRequestResponse
ListWorkers

List Workers.

 ateapi.ListWorkersRequest ateapi.ListWorkersResponse
GetWorker

Get a Worker.

 ateapi.GetWorkerRequest ateapi.Worker
CreateWorker

Register a Worker. Called once its Pod is Ready and has an IP.

 ateapi.CreateWorkerRequest ateapi.Worker
UpdateWorker

Update observed pool state on a Worker.

 ateapi.UpdateWorkerRequest ateapi.Worker
DeleteWorker

Deregister a Worker. Does not cascade: the caller is responsible for cleaning up related resources first.

 ateapi.DeleteWorkerRequest ateapi.Worker
DrainWorker

Mark a Worker as terminating so the scheduler stops routing new Actors to it. Idempotent; one-way. Deliberately leaves any bound Actor alone. Returns ABORTED if another write lands on the Worker first; retry.

 ateapi.DrainWorkerRequest ateapi.Worker
ListWorkerActorAssignments

List the Actors hosted by a given Worker.

 ateapi.ListWorkerActorAssignmentsRequest ateapi.ListWorkerActorAssignmentsResponse

status WorkerStatus

Output-only server-managed state. Absent from Create/Update request payloads; whatever a request carries here is ignored. DrainWorker is the only way a client moves state, and the assignments are the scheduler's.

+k8s:optional

status.state WorkerState

+k8s:required +k8s:minimum=1 +k8s:maximum=2 # keep this in sync with the WorkerState enum

status.capacity WorkerResources

The total resource capacity of the Worker.

A Worker should report every dimension of resources it has available to be consumed by Actors. Any resource not specified here is assumed to be 0. An Actor which requests a resource which is not present in a Worker's capacity will prevent that Actor from running on that Worker.

Shrinking capacity below allocated prevents new placements but does not evicts running Actors.

+k8s:optional

status.capacity.resources Resources

Resources match the Actor's definition of resources. They are matched by name and used for placement.

+k8s:optional

status.capacity.resources.limits repeated Limits

limits is the maximum amount of compute resources allowed. Only "cpu" and "memory" are supported, each at most once, and each quantity must be greater than zero; the cpu limit must be less than 1000 cores.

+k8s:optional +k8s:maxItems=2 +k8s:listType=map +k8s:listMapKey=name +k8s:customValidation # names, quantity parse/positivity, cpu bound

status.capacity.resources.limits.name string

+k8s:required +k8s:maxLength=16 # the hook on Resources.limits restricts values to cpu/memory

status.capacity.resources.limits.quantity string

quantity is in Kubernetes resource.Quantity string form (e.g. "500m", "2Gi").

+k8s:required +k8s:maxLength=32 # the hook on Resources.limits requires a parseable quantity

status.capacity.actors int32

A count of Actors. Workers can use this to limit the number of Actors that can be placed on them, constraining the costs of other things that are not captured in the resources above, but which still have costs - netns, mounts, file descriptors, etc.

+k8s:optional +k8s:minimum=1

status.allocated WorkerResources

The allocated resources of the Worker. This is the sum of all the resources consumed by the Actors currently assigned to this Worker.

+k8s:optional

status.allocated.resources Resources

Resources match the Actor's definition of resources. They are matched by name and used for placement.

+k8s:optional

status.allocated.resources.limits repeated Limits

limits is the maximum amount of compute resources allowed. Only "cpu" and "memory" are supported, each at most once, and each quantity must be greater than zero; the cpu limit must be less than 1000 cores.

A Worker should report every dimension of resources it has available to be consumed by Actors. Any resource not specified here is assumed to be 0. An Actor which requests a resource which is not present in a Worker's capacity will prevent that Actor from running on that Worker.

+k8s:optional

status.capacity.resources.limits repeated Limits

UpdateWorker

Update observed pool state on a Worker.

Parameters

worker Worker

The Worker to update. worker.metadata.name identifies which resource to update. atespace is always empty; Workers are global-scoped. worker.metadata.version and worker.metadata.uid are required preconditions.

labels is the only field an update may change. Every other field is replaced with what the request carries, and a field left unset is cleared — so read the Worker, change what you mean to change, and send the whole thing back. A request that alters an immutable field, by changing it or by omitting it, returns INVALID_ARGUMENT naming the field. status is output-only and whatever it carries is ignored.

CreateTagRequest

Request to tag the external snapshot a suspended Actor holds.

The tag captures whichever snapshot the Actor holds when the call runs. An Actor keeps no snapshot history — each suspend replaces the last — so a suspend that lands between taking a snapshot and tagging it moves what gets tagged. That race is inherent and accepted: the tag means "the Actor as of this call", not "the snapshot some earlier suspend returned".

The tag is given its own copy of that snapshot, so it survives the Actor being suspended again or deleted. To retry a create that failed or timed out, delete the tag first, which collects whatever that attempt stranded, and create it again.

+k8s:customValidation # metadata.atespace must match source_actor.atespace

FieldDescriptionTypeBehavior
tag

The tag to create. metadata.atespace, metadata.name, scope and source_actor are honored; metadata.atespace must match source_actor's, and status is ignored on write.

+k8s:required

HostnameRule

HostnameRule matches requests by destination hostname.

FieldDescriptionTypeBehavior
patterns

DNS names, or DNS names with a wildcard "*" in the leftmost label. The rule matches when any pattern matches.

The DNS name must conform to RFC 1034 and RFC 1123. It must be lowercase and must not have a trailing dot.

A wildcard replaces the complete leftmost label. "*.example.com" matches exactly one non-empty label, such as "api.example.com". It does not match "example.com" or "nested.api.example.com". No other wildcard syntax is accepted. A pattern without a wildcard matches only the complete normalized name.

Internationalized names must use their IDNA A-label (punycode) form; no Unicode conversion is performed. URLs, IP addresses, names with ports, malformed DNS names (for example, "foo..example.com"), and more than one trailing dot are invalid.

+k8s:required +k8s:maxItems=256 +k8s:listType=set +k8s:customValidation # format

MintActorJWTResponse

Response message for MintActorJWT

TODO(identity): check why k8s do ":" and not "/" as a seprator for the Subject format

TODO(identity): whats the right format for the subject? kubernetes follow "system:serviceaccount:<namespace>:<name>".

FieldDescriptionTypeBehavior
actor_jwt

Actor JWT. An OIDC Discovery-compatible JWT

Claims:

  • iss: Issuer - a valid URL where a relying party can fetch the OIDC discovery documents.
  • sub: Subject - a string expressing the identity carried in the credential. Format atespaces:${atespace}:actors:${actorname}.
  • aud: Audience - a string identifying the service this token will be used to authenticate to.
  • nbf: Not Before - a numeric unix timestamp
  • exp: Expiration - a numeric unix timestamp
  • iat: Issued At - a numeric unix timestamp
  • ate.dev: Ate/Substrate Extension - JSON object
    • atespace: (string) The atespace the actor belongs to
    • actorName: (string) The actor's name, unique within its atespace
 string

UpdateWorkerRequest

FieldDescriptionTypeBehavior
worker

The Worker to update. worker.metadata.name identifies which resource to update. atespace is always empty; Workers are global-scoped. worker.metadata.version and worker.metadata.uid are required preconditions.

labels is the only field an update may change. Every other field is replaced with what the request carries, and a field left unset is cleared — so read the Worker, change what you mean to change, and send the whole thing back. A request that alters an immutable field, by changing it or by omitting it, returns INVALID_ARGUMENT naming the field. status is output-only and whatever it carries is ignored.

+k8s:required +k8s:opaqueType # updates are handled in 2 steps, do not descend +k8s:subfield(metadata)=+k8s:required +k8s:customValidation # TODO: when we get nested subfields, forbid metadata.atespace

 Worker

WorkerAssignment

WorkerAssignment points at the Worker currently hosting an Actor.

This is a denormalized snapshot, not merely a reference: atenet reads worker_pod_ip on the request-routing path and must not need a second lookup, and kubectl-ate displays the pod name. The copies stay valid for the life of the assignment because a Worker's identity fields are immutable.

Pass worker to GetWorker; none of the denormalized fields identify the Worker to the API.

FieldDescriptionTypeBehavior
worker

worker references the assigned Worker. This is the field to look the Worker up by; the worker_* fields below are a denormalized copy kept so that readers on a hot path do not have to fetch the Worker at all.

Workers are global-scoped, so this carries no atespace.

+k8s:beta(since: "0.0")=+k8s:subfield(atespace)=+k8s:forbidden # TODO: get rid of beta prefix +k8s:required

 ObjectRef
worker_namespace

worker_namespace is the Kubernetes namespace of the WorkerPool and worker Pod.

+k8s:required +k8s:format=k8s-short-name

 string
worker_pool

+k8s:required +k8s:format=k8s-long-name

 string
worker_pod

worker_pod is the name of the Kubernetes pod hosting the Actor.

+k8s:required +k8s:format=k8s-long-name

 string
worker_pod_uid

worker_pod_uid is the Kubernetes UID of worker_pod.

+k8s:required +k8s:format=k8s-uuid

 string
worker_pod_ip

+k8s:required +k8s:customValidation # until format=k8s-ip is supported

WorkerStatus

FieldDescriptionTypeBehavior
state

+k8s:required +k8s:minimum=1 +k8s:maximum=2 # keep this in sync with the WorkerState enum

 WorkerState
capacity

The total resource capacity of the Worker.

A Worker should report every dimension of resources it has available to be consumed by Actors. Any resource not specified here is assumed to be 0. An Actor which requests a resource which is not present in a Worker's capacity will prevent that Actor from running on that Worker.

Shrinking capacity below allocated prevents new placements but does not evicts running Actors.

+k8s:optional

 WorkerResources
allocated

The allocated resources of the Worker. This is the sum of all the resources consumed by the Actors currently assigned to this Worker.

+k8s:optional
